title: Gaza students return to in-person schooling
content:
Hundreds of thousands of children in Gaza returned to in-person teaching for the first time in nearly three years, albeit in damaged or makeshift school buildings and tents, and with uniforms, notebooks and pens unaffordable for many families.
The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) says 98% of schools in Gaza were either destroyed or damaged during the war, and Gaza education officials say about 660,000 students have been deprived of in-person learning and regular participation in education.
The reopening on Saturday is a fragile milestone for Gaza after a conflict that has killed around 22,000 students and more than 770 education workers, including 532 teachers, according to the director of education for East Khan Younis.
"The last time I have been to school was three years ago. Now, we are starting the school year, it is year of joy, happiness and success," said one student in Khan Younis.
Another boy said he was determined to learn even though he will sit on the floor in a tent lacking ventilation, he has no decent shoes, nor a notebook and pen, and lost friends during the war.
"Despite all of this we will learn, we will learn even in a tent."
Fifteen-year-old displaced student Samar Abu Salmi, who lives with her family in a tent, is also returning to class.
"We studied on phones and we haven't seen our teachers...now, we are back pursuing our dream... from one tent to another," she said, speaking in the yard of her new makeshift school.
She also lacks much of the essential equipment, which has become unaffordable for her family.
"Before the war, everything was available for us - notebooks, pens, goods, clothes, outings, things that we could get cheaply," Salmi said.
Despite the devastation in Gaza, the Ministry of Education, backed by international and local organisations, has moved ahead with the 2026-27 academic year, establishing dozens of temporary schools made of tents, tarpaulins, sheet metal and wood to accommodate pupils.
Some are built on sandy ground, others have classrooms with only some mattresses and a blackboard, into which students cram. Others are still housing dozens of displaced families.
At least 540,000 students are expected to attend in-person classes this year in makeshift private schools, temporary learning centres and educational points, with UNICEF support, according to education officials.
Online learning will continue for those who cannot attend classes or who left Gaza during the war.

title: African youth test Mars rovers at Sansa’s Hartebeesthoek Mars Yard
content:
Beyond robots, the test empowered African youth to solve real challenges and shape the future of space exploration.
Africa’s young innovators turned Hartebeesthoek into a Martian frontier this weekend, as 18 finalist teams battled terrain, technology and time in the Cars4Mars African Rover Challenge Mars Stage Final 2026.
Hosted at the South African National Space Agency’s (Sansa) Mars Yard, the competition drew more than 120 participants from South Africa, Kenya and Zimbabwe.
Five-month challenge
They were the best of nearly 100 teams from 11 African countries who entered the five‑month challenge, which began on 1 May and culminated in Saturday’s final.
The rovers faced two missions: the Traversal Mission, requiring remote navigation across uneven terrain while transporting objects, and the AI Autonomous Mission, where teams applied computer vision to identify items such as hammers, tennis balls and coloured balloons.
Extra points were awarded for systems that could pinpoint object locations.
Skill
Cars4Mars founder Basia Nasiorowska said the day showcased grit as much as skill
“We saw wheels come off, AI systems falter, and teams forced to improvise. Yet they kept going. That perseverance is what stood out most. By the end, they had overcome obstacles and completed their missions. Every participant should be proud of the determination and creativity they showed.”
Judged by an international panel, the rovers were tested on a Mars Yard built from 40 tonnes of red sand sponsored by Afrimat to replicate Martian terrain.
Top honours
Top honours went to Cyberstorm from Milestone High School in Zimbabwe, followed by Inadeptus Mechanicus from Rhodes and Stellenbosch Universities, and Tech Tonic from Bryanston High School.
Special awards recognised excellence in AI, traversal, design and creativity, while all other finalists received Perseverance Awards.
Winners walked away with Creality 3D printers, RS South Africa vouchers and 3D‑printed trophies.
A wide range of partners backed the event, including SMD Technologies, Scientific Technical Labs, MSI ZA, Stelltron, ER24 and Vision Dynamics.
African youth
Sansa said the partnership cements Hartebeesthoek as the permanent venue for future finals.
“This is about more than robots. It’s about giving African youth the chance to solve real challenges and see themselves as part of the future of space exploration,” Nasiorowska added.

title: As mulheres que ajudaram a construir o São João de Caruaru
content: <_cdata>Pouco lembradas, cantoras contribuíram para que cidade pernambucana se tornasse a ‘capital do forró’ Em 1978, Joana Angélica lançava seu primeiro álbum, intitulado “Forró”, dando início a uma trajetória que marca o gênero na região Arquivo Pessoal / Nonada/OVA O São João de Caruaru, a “capital do forró”, é conhecido mundialmente. Isso se deve aos inúmeros artistas que a cidade gesta e que a cantam. A festa que começou como confraternização entre vizinhos, movimentou em 2026 R$ 805 milhões e hoje conta com polos temáticos espalhados por todo o município: o Pátio de Eventos Luiz Lua Gonzaga, o Polo Azulão, o Alto do Moura, o Polo do Pífano (Sebastião Biano), o Polo de Repente (Poeta Lídio Cavalcanti), o Polo Mestre Camarão, o Polo Rildo Hora e o Polo Juarez Santana — todos em homenagem a homens. Seria isso um indicativo da ausência de mulheres na cena? Para responder a essa pergunta, o Nonada, em parceria com o Observatório da Vida Agreste (OVA), conversou com as cantoras Joana Angélica, Marlene do Forró e Vitória do Pife, todas caruaruenses. Enquanto a festa entra no calendário dos grandes eventos do Brasil e se torna um dos principais motores econômicos de Pernambuco, as mulheres que ajudaram a construir essa história parecem viver uma outra realidade. Em 1977, quando ainda era realizada na rua 3 de maio, no centro, a festa foi comandada pelas irmãs Lira – Eulina, Juraci, Laurinda, Adélia, Odília e Marinete, “as precursoras do São João de rua na capital do forró”, segundo matéria do jornal Vanguarda de Caruaru. Elas organizaram a estrutura da festa, os ornamentos e a grade dos artistas por 21 anos, angariando apoio dos vizinhos e comerciantes locais, sem apoio público. Esse modelo de festa organizado por elas — no mês de junho, perto do dia de São João, 24, com rua enfeitada, de graça, com a presença de artistas locais e de outros lugares cantando em um palco para o povo dançar, assistir quadrilhas, arranjar casamento e comer — foi o embrião para a festa que hoje dura 70 dias e recebe 4 milhões de pessoas (duas vezes a população de Curitiba). Marinete (87), última das irmãs Lira viva e que ainda mora na rua 3 de maio, conta o porquê elas decidiram fazer a festa: “A gente era festeira, gostava de namorar e pensamos ‘vamos fazer’”. As irmãs Lira eram 8, mas só 6 participaram da organização. Marinete explica: “As outras duas eram casadas”. Depois de 20 anos de êxito, a festa da rua 3 de maio sofreu com a falta de apoio financeiro. “A prefeitura [de Caruaru] chamou a gente para uma reunião”, conta Marinete, “não fazia sentido querer competir com eles.” A festa, então, passou a ser realizada na rua Rui Barbosa e depois no Pátio de Eventos Luiz Lua Gonzaga, onde é realizada até hoje. Em paralelo a esse cenário, a cantora Joana Angélica (78) iniciava sua carreira solo gravando seu primeiro álbum intitulado Forró, lançado em 1978. Já Marlene do Forró (59), a geração seguinte de Joana, passava as tardes ouvindo a pioneira Marinês no rádio: a cantora foi o estopim que fez Marlene cantar. As cantoras da nova geração, como Vitória do Pife (26), nem poderiam imaginar que essas seriam as mulheres que abririam caminho para que elas pudessem cantar forró. A contribuição das irmãs Lira na produção da festa ressoa numa fala de Joana sobre o início da sua carreira na bandinha do Mestre Camarão, importante sanfoneiro da cidade. “No começo, não tinha mulher [cantando em bandas de forró]. Camarão me escondia, tudo porque ninguém queria mulher nas bandas, era só homem”. Última das irmãs Lira viva, Marinete conta com orgulho sobre o protagonismo e o pioneirismo das mulheres no São João de Caruaru Lucas Bezerra / Nonada/OVA Joana Angélica, que ainda se chamava Risoleide Alves, nome de batismo, cresceu cercada por música: o pai tocava violão e a mãe cantava. Aos 8 anos, cantou com Cauby Peixoto no antigo teatro do Círculo Operário, em Caruaru, onde hoje funciona um supermercado. Ela conta que estava passando em frente ao teatro, de pés descalços, quando ouviu Cauby chamar por uma criança que cantasse sua música. “Eu passei pelas pernas do segurança na portaria e fui bater no palco. Falei que sabia cantar a música dele e ele me chamou no palco.” Ela relembra que ele se ajoelhou na frente dela, como na letra de Nono Mandamento, música que ela cantou na ocasião. A coragem lhe rendeu um sapato Sete Vidas, um corte de tecido, um conto de réis e a possibilidade de um futuro nos palcos. Joana conta as histórias que estão nesta reportagem sentada em uma cadeira de rodas elétrica, na sala de entrada da sua casa, que funciona como um pequeno museu da sua vida, no bairro Kennedy, em Caruaru. Os vários quadros pendurados com fotos de momentos importantes da sua carreira e certificados de honrarias recebidas ao longo da vida, são um indicativo do passado vivido. Já o perfume refrescante que exala dela, o vestido colorido e decotado que ela usa, os brincos grandes nas orelhas, a leve maquiagem no rosto, as unhas pintadas, o cabelo recém lavado e finalizado, são um indicativo da Joana do presente, de 78 anos, que se adapta à ausência de parte da perna direita, perdida em um acidente há menos de um ano. “Mas, eu só disse que era cantora quando eu ganhei meu primeiro cachê, lá em Vertentes [município pernambucano], no circo. Eu tinha 14 anos”. Ela passou a acompanhar o irmão sanfoneiro, Zé Bicudo, e a se apresentar em caravanas, em cima de caminhões e em circos. Aos 19, cruza por coincidência – ou não – com o Mestre Camarão dentro de um ônibus com destino a Caruaru. A essa altura, a Bandinha do Camarão já acumulava discos e parcerias com Dominguinhos, Luiz Gonzaga e Hermeto Pascoal. ‘Só tem polo para homem’ “Cantei 30 anos na Bandinha do Camarão e [com ele] viajei o Brasil inteiro”. Joana era a cantora da banda, que até então, era apenas instrumental. Camarão é um dos responsáveis por popularizar a sanfona no forró e por introduzir metais – trompete, saxofone – e guitarra. Instrumentos que hoje são comuns em bandas de forró. Risoleide Alves morreu, como ela mesma diz, no estúdio Esquema, na Avenida Brasil, no Rio de Janeiro, em 1978, para que Joana Angélica pudesse vir ao mundo. Quem fez o parto foi Luiz Gonzaga. Ela conta que alguém no estúdio chamou a cantora de Caruaru. Gonzaga perguntou o que ela cantava e, ao saber que era forró, estranhou: “Eu não acredito que uma cantora de Caruaru vai gravar forró com esse nome. Cadê ela?” Quando a falecida Risoleide se aproximou, ele a reconheceu: “Ah, eu já te conheço, você é ‘meia banda’.” Ela perguntou por quê, e ele explicou: “Porque na banda de Camarão você canta uma noite todinha.” Em seguida, fez uma sugestão: “Você gravando com esse nome de Risoleide, você não vai gravar forró, vai gravar bolero. Se você aceitar, a partir de hoje, seu nome pode ser Joana. Santa Joana é a protetora dos artistas, protetora do nordestino.” Joana aceitou na hora: “Risoleide não tá mais aqui, não!” No ano seguinte, 1979, gravou o seu segundo disco, o ‘Forró Bom’, na mesma gravadora. Em 1980, gravou o terceiro e seguiu assim até gravar outros 16 álbuns solo. Ela passou a se dividir entre os shows solo e os da banda de Camarão, que insistia em sua permanência por “não encontrar outra cantora no mesmo nível”. Depois da repercussão positiva do segundo álbum, Joana tomou a decisão de sair de vez da banda de Camarão e de Caruaru. Ela se deu conta de que, apesar de ser conhecida popularmente como a rainha do forró, por ser uma das únicas cantoras de Caruaru, vivia na sombra de Camarão. “Você só tá dando nome pra Camarão. Você é jovem, você tem tudo pela frente”, relembra o conselho que ouviu de Abdias, esposo da cantora Marinês. “Aí, a mulher dele, Marinês, chegou pra mim e disse ‘sua voz tem peso em todo estilo de música, agora no forró é o peso”. A partir desse momento, ela começa a viajar pelo Brasil sozinha. Reconhecida como Patrimônio Vivo do município, Joana Angélica tem 16 álbuns solo lançados Arquivo pessoal / Nonada/OVA “Eu fui embora daqui, não fiquei. Fui pra São Paulo, fui pro Rio [de Janeiro], fui pro Paraná. Voltei pra João Pessoa, morei em Natal, fui pra Bahia, fiquei na cidade de São Sebastião do Passé, fazendo minha história.” Pelo caminho, conheceu inúmeras pessoas, se apresentou no Brilho da Lua em São Paulo, e dividiu o palco com grandes nomes da música brasileira – Roberta Miranda, Nelson Gonçalves e Agnaldo Timóteo. Após anos fora, Joana decidiu retornar a Caruaru, em busca do reconhecimento em sua terra natal que sempre lhe escapou. “Eu voltei porque eu não vim mais fazer história, eu voltei pra minha terra”. Em 2017, ela foi uma das homenageadas do São João de Caruaru, ano em que completava 50 anos de carreira. Em 2020, se tornou “Patrimônio Vivo” do município. Em março de 2026, recebeu a Medalha de Honra ao Mérito “Luiz Gonzaga” da Câmara Municipal de Caruaru, como reconhecimento formal de sua contribuição à cultura popular. Apesar dos títulos, a sensação de Joana é de que a cidade ainda não a valoriza. Cachês desproporcionais em relação aos pagos a cantores de outros estilos musicais apontam que a festa se tornou um grande negócio que privilegia artistas de fora, enquanto os locais são deixados de lado. “Só vou me sentir [valorizada] no dia que tiver o primeiro polo feminino, que não tem. Só tem polo de homem, e que esse polo [se chame] Joana Angélica. Aí eu vou me sentir realizada. E outra coisa, eu quero um polo eu em vida, pra inaugurar, participar e convidar minhas amigas cantoras pra inaugurar.” Vozes à margem A sensação de desvalorização também é compartilhada por Marlene do Forró, que conversou conosco por telefone, entre os horários de visita à irmã internada no hospital e as demandas da própria vida. O seu tom de voz na ligação era de quem teve que resolver diversas questões ao longo do dia e que, naquele momento, às 19h12, tinha que parar para responder perguntas de um jornalista desconhecido sobre a sua infância. As histórias que Marlene se pôs a repetir, não são apenas dela, são três décadas da história de uma cidade inteira. Para Marlene, a cidade que ainda é seu palco e a consagrou como uma das vozes femininas do forró é a mesma que, nos últimos anos, a empurra para a margem. “Caruaru não dá valor a ninguém”, comenta ela enquanto relembra a agenda lotada de shows dos anos 90. Ela se refere a preferência por parte dos organizadores atuais do São João de Caruaru por cantores de outros estilos musicais — axé, sertanejo universitário, pagode e eletrônico — para se apresentar no palco principal do São João, pagos com cachês milionários. Enquanto os artistas locais precisam esperar meses para receber um valor que se aproxima do simbólico, quando comparado a um milhão e quinhentos mil reais que o cantor Wesley Safadão recebeu por se apresentar este ano. “Meu pai ligava o rádio quando eu era pequena. Eu escutava Marinês e dizia ‘que gogó essa mulher tem’” e como um pássaro que aprende as melodias da espécie ouvindo os adultos, Marlene aprendeu a cantar ouvindo Marinês no rádio, como ela mesma diz. Marinês, “o estopim da bomba”, impulsionou a jovem Marlene a cantar e a participar do programa de calouro da Rádio Difusora de Caruaru, na primeira metade dos anos 80. Cantando De Volta pro Aconchego, de Dominguinhos, ela garantiu o primeiro lugar e um novo rumo para sua vida. O sucesso se repetiu na Festa do Comércio, realizada na rua 15 de novembro, no centro de Caruaru, quando, novamente, venceu o concurso de calouros cantando a mesma música. Depois disso, foi impedida de participar de programas de calouro, pois, “já era cantora”. “Até hoje em dia”, conta ela, enquanto sorri “De Volta pro Aconchego é o hino do meu repertório queira ou não queira”. Vencer esses concursos tornou Marlene visada por diversas bandas de forró da cidade. Ela recebeu propostas de várias bandas e passou a se apresentar em quatro diferentes na mesma semana, apenas trocando de roupa entre um show e outro. Esse período foi crucial para ela desenvolver seu estilo próprio, utilizando instrumentos como o fuzileiro – um bumbo de percussão usado principalmente em fanfarras – e criando figurinos exclusivos para cada show. “O estilo [das roupas] eu mesmo que desenho, eu mesmo que boto os enfeites, mando a costureira botar. Já pra ficar uma coisa diferente”. Cores, diferentes tecidos combinados, lantejoulas, pedrarias, franjas, corset, botas e chapéus, são elementos obrigatórios nos figurinos dela. Joana Angélica Lucas Bezerra / Nonada/OVA Sua carreira deslanchou quando foi a cantora oficial da Banda Lilás, de Zé de Oliveira, importante músico da cidade, onde permaneceu por cerca de sete anos, e na Banda Régis. “Eu carregava a banda Régis nas minhas costas. Ele bebia muito, fumava muito. Agora, era um grande músico. Um sanfoneiro que até hoje eu não encontrei igual”, relembra Marlene. Nessas últimas, Marlene cantava de tudo, do forró ao brega, tendo em vista que era uma funcionária. No final dos anos 90, as primeiras bandas de forró universitário estavam explodindo, Mastruz Com Leite, por exemplo. Ela conta que o público pedia as músicas deles que foram, invariavelmente, incorporadas ao repertório. “[A gente fazia] muito show. Tinha espaço para essas bandas que não tinham nome”, recorda ela sobre o final dos anos 90. “A gente ganhava muito dinheiro, graças a Deus, e viajava muito. Hoje não. Hoje só faz show mesmo quem tem conhecimento, mesmo sem nome, sem sucesso”, continua ela. No início dos anos 2000, ela fundou a banda Vaqueiro do Asfalto, em homenagem ao pai, que era vaqueiro. Marlene se apresenta até hoje com essa banda. A experiência nesses grupos fixou o nome de Marlene como uma presença obrigatória nos palcos de Caruaru e região. O reconhecimento veio em 2007, quando recebeu o Troféu Ouro, uma honraria tradicionalmente concedida a políticos e empresários de Caruaru. Em 2019, foi uma das homenageadas do São João de Caruaru, título que recebeu com sentimentos conflitantes. “Foi o ano em que minha mãe faleceu.” Em 2024, recebeu o Troféu Onildo Almeida. Onildo é o compositor da música A Feira de Caruaru, eternizada na voz de Luiz Gonzaga. Acervo de Joana Angélica Lucas Bezerra / Nonada/OVA Apesar da carreira intensa, Marlene nunca viveu exclusivamente da música. Durante grande parte de sua vida, trabalhou como costureira e em escritórios durante o dia, indo para os palcos apenas à noite. A responsabilidade de ajudar a família, especialmente após a morte do pai e para cuidar da mãe, fez com que ela mantivesse essa dupla jornada por muitos anos. Com naturalidade, ela conta: “meus pais criaram a gente trabalhando”. Atualmente, dá aulas de música em sua casa e presta serviços de limpeza no Cemitério Dom Bosco, em Caruaru. Forrozeiras do agora Marlene ganhou o aposto “do Forró” do colunista social Jota Lagos, “e pegou do jeito que não tem como tirar não, né?”, relembra. Ganhar um outro nome ou aposto parece ser uma tradição e requisito. É uma espécie de autorização. Foi assim com Joana, Marlene e também foi assim com a cantora Vitória do Pife. Mas no caso dela, o aposto foi autoimposto. “Eu já fabricava pífanos, eu já dava aula e já tocava, mais ou menos bem, e aí eu mudei meu nome”, conta a jovem forrozeira. O pífano é uma pequena flauta transversal de som agudo, geralmente feito de bambu, taboca ou PVC, que chegou ao Brasil com a invasão portuguesa e foi incorporado à cultura popular, principalmente no Nordeste, ao longo dos séculos. O pífano é considerado por pesquisadores e músicos um ‘movimento ancestral do forró’, especialmente do forró pé de serra — produzido pela junção da sanfona, zabumba e triângulo. Em Caruaru, essa herança é particularmente forte. A centenária Banda de Pífanos de Caruaru e o mestre João do Pife, que ensinou Vitória, são exemplos disso. Vitória conta que o gosto pela música começou logo cedo, mas sua relação com o pífano veio por acaso. “Eu pedi pro meu pai um violão de presente. Na época ele não tinha condições. Daí, ele me levou na oficina do senhor João do Pife e eu tive um hiperfoco.” O mestre a recebeu com alegria, escolheu o instrumento para ela e, em pouco tempo, Vitória já visitava o espaço frequentemente. “Comecei a fazer pífano de PVC em casa, pesquisando no YouTube e aí eu levava para ele [seu João]. Ele viu isso e disse ‘vou ensinar a fazer o pífano de taboca’”. Tanto sozinha, em show solo, em participações, quanto na Banda de Pífanos Caruaru Camaleão, montada por ela e amigos, composta por pífano, prato, fuzileiro e alfaia, às vezes, mais de uma. Além dos grandes mestres pifeiros e da jurema sagrada, onde é feita, Vitória conta: “Tive muita inspiração do trabalho do Metá Metá, Juçara Marçal, Kiko Dinucci, Siba, Renata Rosa. É um pessoal que justamente bebeu da fonte da cultura popular e faz parte da cultura popular, mas que também inova no seu trabalho, traz sua identidade.” Ela tem um álbum lançado, o Sem Pergaminho, que é o resultado das referências e do jeito dela fazer música. Ela enxerga a tradição como algo vivo, que se reinventa a cada dia e que sofre a influência de quem a faz. “Não acho que o forró morreu e nem que está se descaracterizando. O que acontece é que hoje em dia a gente tem muito acesso à mídia e a gente vê muita coisa. E, às vezes, a gente vê mais de uma coisa do que de outra. Muitas vezes é o forró estilizado que está na mídia. Não estou dizendo que um seja melhor nem pior que o outro. O pífano a gente não vê na mídia, mas o pífano está aí” diz Vitória. O que também está presente na mídia e fora dela é o machismo. Segundo ela, ser mulher é um grito de resistência. “Muitas vezes você se sente um pouco só. Muitas vezes você percebe algumas coisas, alguns comportamentos, sejam para querer diminuir a sua presença, seja para diminuir o seu talento, o seu esforço.” O trocadilho – vitória do pife – representa, para ela, uma aposta: “Espero que seja o pife vencendo”. Acrescentamos: e as mulheres também.

title: Asamblea aprueba pago sin multas ni intereses de impuestos municipales en todo El Salvador
content:
Asamblea aprueba pago sin multas ni intereses de impuestos municipales en todo El Salvador
Una ley aprobada por la Asamblea permitirá regularizar impuestos municipales pendientes con dispensa de multas e intereses durante un período de 120 días.
La Asamblea Legislativa aprobó este 17 de septiembre, con 60 votos, una ley transitoria que permitirá a personas naturales y empresas de los 44 municipios de El Salvador ponerse al día con deudas de impuestos municipales sin cancelar multas ni intereses moratorios, además de solicitar planes de pago. El beneficio entrará en vigencia después de que la normativa sea publicada en el Diario Oficial.
La normativa se denomina Ley Especial Transitoria que Otorga Facilidades para el Cumplimiento Voluntario de Obligaciones Sustantivas y Formales en Materia de Impuestos Municipales y establece condiciones específicas para quienes quieran acogerse al beneficio.
Uno de los requisitos es que la obligación tributaria pendiente corresponda, como máximo, al ejercicio fiscal 2025. Además, para acceder a la dispensa de mora e intereses, el contribuyente deberá realizar inicialmente un pago de al menos el 30 % del impuesto pendiente.
La medida tendrá una duración de 120 días continuos, contados a partir de su entrada en vigencia tras la publicación en el Diario Oficial. Ese será el período disponible para que los contribuyentes que cumplan los requisitos soliciten el beneficio.
¿Cómo se podrá pagar la deuda?
Los interesados podrán acudir a los puntos de atención que habilite cada municipalidad para realizar el trámite. La normativa también contempla la posibilidad de efectuar pagos mediante transferencias bancarias, de acuerdo con los mecanismos establecidos.
Además del pago de una parte inicial de la deuda, la ley permite solicitar planes de pago para cancelar las obligaciones municipales pendientes.
Este mecanismo implica también una condición para conservar el beneficio: si el contribuyente incumple el pago de una cuota, perderá las facilidades otorgadas y la municipalidad podrá exigir el pago total de la deuda mediante la vía judicial.
La dispensa permitirá eliminar las multas e intereses moratorios contemplados por la normativa, pero el contribuyente deberá cancelar el impuesto municipal que tiene pendiente bajo las condiciones establecidas.
¿Quiénes podrán solicitar el beneficio?
La normativa incluye a contribuyentes que acumulen multas e intereses debido al pago pendiente de impuestos municipales. También comprende casos relacionados con declaraciones pendientes o incumplimientos de determinadas obligaciones formales.
Sin embargo, no todas las deudas podrán acogerse al régimen. Quedan fuera quienes hayan sido sancionados mediante un procedimiento de determinación tributaria de oficio y aquellos contra quienes la municipalidad ya haya iniciado un proceso judicial para recuperar lo adeudado.
La ley abarca los 44 municipios del país, por lo que las personas naturales y jurídicas que cumplan las condiciones podrán gestionar el beneficio ante la municipalidad correspondiente durante el período establecido.
Para los contribuyentes, ponerse al día también puede ser relevante para recuperar su solvencia municipal, un documento que puede ser requerido para determinados trámites y operaciones.
Los 44 municipios beneficiados
- Ahuachapán: Ahuachapán Norte, Ahuachapán Centro y Ahuachapán Sur.
- San Salvador: San Salvador Norte, San Salvador Oeste, San Salvador Este, San Salvador Centro y San Salvador Sur.
- La Libertad: La Libertad Norte, La Libertad Centro, La Libertad Oeste, La Libertad Este, La Libertad Costa y La Libertad Sur.
- Chalatenango: Chalatenango Norte, Chalatenango Centro y Chalatenango Sur.
- Cuscatlán: Cuscatlán Norte y Cuscatlán Sur.
- Cabañas: Cabañas Este y Cabañas Oeste.
- La Paz: La Paz Oeste, La Paz Centro y La Paz Este.
- La Unión: La Unión Norte y La Unión Sur.
- Usulután: Usulután Norte, Usulután Este y Usulután Oeste.
- Sonsonate: Sonsonate Norte, Sonsonate Centro, Sonsonate Este y Sonsonate Oeste.
- Santa Ana: Santa Ana Norte, Santa Ana Centro, Santa Ana Este y Santa Ana Oeste.
- San Vicente: San Vicente Norte y San Vicente Sur.
- San Miguel: San Miguel Norte, San Miguel Centro y San Miguel Oeste.
- Morazán: Morazán Norte y Morazán Sur.
San Salvador acumula $136 millones en intereses
Durante el estudio previo de la iniciativa en la Comisión de Hacienda, los diputados recibieron a los alcaldes de San Salvador Centro, Mario Durán; La Libertad Sur, Henry Flores; y Santa Ana Oeste, Jorge Castro, quienes expusieron información sobre las deudas acumuladas en las municipalidades.
Durán señaló que San Salvador Centro registra aproximadamente $136 millones en intereses relacionados con obligaciones pendientes. Según los cálculos presentados por el alcalde, al dispensar esos recargos la comuna podría recuperar alrededor de $59 millones correspondientes a impuestos adeudados.
Durante esa discusión también se planteó que las facilidades pueden beneficiar a personas jurídicas que necesitan regularizar sus obligaciones municipales para obtener una solvencia y realizar determinadas operaciones.
El alcalde de La Libertad Sur, Henry Flores, indicó durante el análisis de la iniciativa que recuperar estos recursos permitiría destinarlos a servicios y proyectos municipales, entre ellos trabajos en mercados, bacheo y alumbrado público.
¿Desde cuándo se podrá solicitar?
Aunque la Asamblea ya aprobó la normativa, los 120 días no comienzan a contarse desde la votación legislativa. La ley establece que entrará en vigencia después de su publicación en el Diario Oficial.
A partir de esa entrada en vigencia comenzará el período establecido para acogerse a la dispensa de multas e intereses y solicitar las facilidades correspondientes.
Por ello, quienes tengan impuestos municipales pendientes deberán verificar que su deuda cumpla con los requisitos, especialmente que corresponda como máximo al ejercicio 2025, y consultar los mecanismos de atención y pago que habilite su municipalidad.
La medida será temporal: una vez concluido el plazo de 120 días establecido en la normativa, finalizará la posibilidad de acogerse a estas facilidades bajo este régimen especial.

title: Imádják, hogy salátát keverhetnek maguknak, de kiborulnak, ha nem marad bolognai spagetti
content:
Imádják, hogy salátát keverhetnek maguknak, de kiborulnak, ha nem marad bolognai spagetti
Nagy várakozásokkal fogadta mindenki a szabadszedéses menzákat, amikor a Hungast 2024-ben bejelentette, hogy kiterjeszti az egy évvel korábban még szűkebb körben tesztelt rendszert. Sokan várták, hogy ettől majd jobban esznek a gyerekek, és esetleg kevesebb élelmiszer-hulladék termelődik. De tényleg megváltotta a generációk óta utált hazai menzarendszert a svédasztal? Mivel egyre több iskolában vezették be az utóbbi évben, összeszedtük a tapasztalatokat, amihez iskolai vezetőkkel és a leginkább érintettekkel, gyerekkel is beszéltünk.
Dani (10) úgy képzelte, hogy a szabadszedéses menza olyasmi lesz, mint a svédasztalos szállodai vacsora, ezért elsőre csalódott volt. Annak örül, hogy van lehetősége zöldséget és salátát szedni, üresen enni a rizst és a tésztát, illetve ha ízlik neki a leves, akkor vehet kétszer. A zöldségeknek a várakozásokkal ellentétben szinte minden, általunk megkérdezett gyerek örül, főleg azért, mert azt is kiválaszthatják, melyik zöldségből szednek. Egyikük inkább a paradicsomot, másikuk az uborkát szereti, és most már mindenki maga dönthet. Előfordulnak persze viták a salátabár körül, ha valaki kiszedi az összes kukoricát.
Kinga (12) panaszkodott, hogy a kisebbek mehetnek előbb ebédelni, így a nagyobb évfolyamosoknak néha csak egymáshoz nem illő elemek jutnak. Ez a leggyakoribb panasz: halrudacskára készülnek, de csak pásztortarhonya marad, így csalódottak. Ugyanakkor több gyerek is büszkélkedett azzal, hogy korábban utált ételeket kedvelt meg, mivel volt arra lehetősége, hogy megkóstolja, és aztán döntse el, szeretne-e belőle még.
Berci (9) úgy véli, az nem szabadság, hogyha nem szedhet bármiből azt, ami neki szimpatikus, hanem azt kell a tányérjára kanalaznia, amit a mintaadagra rajzoltak. Szeretné másképp kombinálni az elemeket, például a főzelékfeltétnek szánt fasírthoz nem főzeléket, hanem rizst enni, de ezt nem engedik. Tomi (8) szerint viszont lehet ügyeskedni, ha épp kedves a konyhás néni. Kati (13) szülei szerint a szabadszedéses menza nagy hatalmat adott a konyhás néniknek, így minden attól függ, ők hogyan állnak ehhez.
Miki (10) szerint annyira kell rohanni, hogy nincs ideje átgondolni, mit szeretne, ezért mindig biztosra megy, gyorsan eszik egy kevés rizst, és rohan tovább, így viszont éhes marad, és a délutáni edzés előtt túlárazott rántott húsos szendvicseket kell vásárolnia. Mivel a konyhás nénik arra biztatják őket, hogy keveset szedjenek, ezért alig mer venni. A levest kapásból kihagyja, mert azt mondja, nem lenne ideje újra sorba állni a másodikért. Sokszor van rántott zöldség, amit utál, ilyenkor is köretet eszik, vagy persze tejbegrízt, ha épp az a desszert. Laci (11) viszont imádja a salátabárt, olyan zöldségeket eszik, amiket otthon soha, gyakran repetázik, és a minap kipróbálta a tócsnit, amit korábban sosem evett még.
Sok zöldség és népszerű halrudacska
Sódarné Bakos Barbara, az V. kerületi Hild József Általános Iskola igazgatója szerint a gyerekek örömmel fogadták az új rendszert, bár még csak pár havi tesztüzemen vannak túl. A kerületi iskolákban a szabad szedés úgy működik, hogy nem a szülő választja ki rendeléskor, hanem a gyerekek a kínálat alapján dönthetik el, melyik ételt eszik. Több meglepő jelenséget is észleltek. Például azt gondolták, hogy a vegetáriánus menü nem lesz népszerű, mégis sokan szívesen választják azt is. Előfordult, hogy hamarabb fogyott el a gombapaprikás, mint a csirkeragu. Örülnek a salátabárnak, amivel kapcsolatban mindenki szkeptikus volt. Nemcsak a kukorica fogy, hanem a répa és a paradicsom is, szeretik az önteteket, kombinálják a zöldségeket, így biztosan nőtt a gyerekek zöldségfogyasztása.
Vannak nehézségek is, amiket szervezési variációkkal próbálnak kiküszöbölni. Például azt a problémát, hogy a slágerételek hamarabb elfogynak, mint a többi opció, és ha mindenki ugyanazt eszi, akkor a konyhás nénik korlátozni kezdik a mennyiséget, hogy mindenkinek jusson. A konyháról aztán a szolgáltatóhoz visszajuttatják ezeket a tanulságokat, ami ezek alapján próbálja a népszerűséghez igazítani a mennyiségeket. A visszajelzések nyomán például a halrudacska, ami nagy kedvenc, most a menü két elemében is szerepel, csak a köret más. Akkor sem marad éhes senki, ha például a bolognai spagettiből enne még, de repeta már nem jut neki, olyankor repetázhat valami mást – mondta az igazgatónő.
Nekik egyelőre egy olyan, az órarendekhez passzoló ebédrend kialakítása a kihívás, ami alapján úgy oszthatják be a gyerekeket, hogy mindenkinek mindegyik választási lehetőségből jusson. Nemcsak a tanrendjük, de az igényeik is mások a felsős nagyobbaknak, mint a legkisebbeknek.
Az új menzarendszerrel együtt emelkedtek az árak is, mégis úgy látják, több gyerek ebédel, mint a korábbi rendszerben, mert a gyerekek szívesebben mennek le, nagyobb kedvvel ebédelnek. Azelőtt gyakran csak benéztek, azt mondták, nem szeretik az aznapi menüt, és meg se kóstolták az ebédet, viszont így, hogy van választási lehetőség, mindig tudnak valamit enni.
Azzal együtt, hogy a Hild József iskolában is sokkal kevesebb az új rendszerben az élelmiszer-maradék, előfordul, hogy nem fogy el minden étel, ezért a hatodik óra után vissza lehet térni akár másodszor ebédelni, repetázni, és ilyenkor már kombinálhatnak bármit bármivel, mivel az a cél, hogy minden elfogyjon. Ezzel a lehetőséggel azonban egyelőre kevesen élnek.
A legkisebbek néha megtorpannak a választási lehetőségek miatt, ilyenkor szükség van a tanító nénikre, el kell magyarázni nekik, hogy melyik ételben mi van, így el tudják dönteni, hogy azt szeretik-e, vagy sem. Az alsósoknál nagy előny a szabadszedéses rendszer abból a szempontból, hogy ehetnek kevesebbet, mert kisebb az étvágyuk. Ez ideális esetben kiegyenlítődik, mivel a nyolcadikosok pedig többet esznek.
Sódarné szerint az ételek minősége is javult, remek, hogy a köretek változatosak, nem mindig rizs és krumpli van csak, hanem például kuszkusz és bulgur is. Ettől függetlenül úgy látja, hogy az otthon válogatós gyerekek itt is válogatósak lesznek. Sokszor azért nem kóstolnak meg valamit, mert nem tetszik nekik, ahogy kinéz, tartanak a gyanús színűnek ítélt raguktól. Azokat az ételeket választják, amiket otthon is kapnak, újat akkor kóstolnak, ha látványra tetszik nekik. Arra is van lehetőség, hogy szedjenek egy picit, megkóstolják, és akkor vegyenek egész adagot, ha ízlik – számolt be a tapasztalatokról az igazgatónő.
A szabad szedés belsőépítészeti kérdés is
A Közgazdasági Politechnikumban korábban menüválasztásos rendszer volt, de a gyerekek nem mindig azt akarták enni, amit a szüleik korábban kiválasztottak nekik – számolt be a tapasztalatokról Kováts Lívia, a IX. kerületi hatosztályos gimnázium ügyvezető koordinátora. Probléma volt az is, hogy gyakran meghagyták az ebédet, sok étel került a kukába. Egy évvel ezelőtt vezették be a szabadszedéses rendszert, és a kérdőívek alapján úgy tűnik, hogy a gyerekek sokkal jobban szeretik. Megkóstolnak olyasmit is, amit korábban nem, például többen is kiemelték, hogy a resztelt májat azelőtt nem ették meg, itt viszont kipróbálták, és ízlett nekik. Kováts Lívia szerint ebben a rendszerben a gyerekek nyitottabbak lesznek a zöldséges, húsmentes ételekre is, mivel van lehetőségük ezeket is kipróbálni.
A szabadszedéses rendszer jórészt belsőépítészeti kérdés: amelyik iskolának van tere a jó elrendezéshez, annak csúcsszuper megoldás, amelyiknek nincs, annak viszont küzdelem. Vannak olyan iskolák, ahol az étkező közepére tudják elhelyezni az ételeket, a pult körbejárható, és nincs sor. Ahol ez nem lehetséges, az nagyon megnehezíti a folyamat lebonyolítását, tumultus alakul ki, bedugul a rendszer, lassú a haladás. Az, hogy mit és mennyit szednek maguknak a gyerekek, attól is függ, milyen hosszan kell sorban állniuk, mennyire férnek hozzá. Sőt: gyakran azért nem jut egyik vagy másik féle fogásból valakinek, mert a konyhás néni nem fér a pulthoz, hogy újratöltse. A helyhiány miatt sorok alakulnak ki, ezért sokan hagyják ki például a leveseket, amik pedig most sokkal jobbak, mint a régi menzás levesek – minőségi kifogás amúgy is ritkán van az ételeket illetően. Annak ellenére, hogy itt a gyerekek már nagyok, szükség van egy ügyeletes tanárra, aki végig koordinál, terelgeti őket. Ahol sok hely van, ott erre sincs szükség.
A gimis gyerekek olykor abból csinálnak versenyt, hogy ki tud nyolc-tíz virslit megenni, miközben a referenciaadag két darab a sárgaborsó-főzelékhez, amiből pedig nem is esznek. Előfordult, hogy mandarinból harminc darabot vitt ki egy gyerek poénból, majd nyilván nem ette meg. Ezért is próbálják arra buzdítani őket, hogy csak annyit vegyenek maguknak, amennyit a minta is mutat. Jó példa a rendszer félresiklására az az eset, amikor a főzelékfeltét zöldséges golyó, amiből a mintaadag három darab. A gyerek nem olvassa el, mi az, azt hiszi róla, hogy fasírt, ezért vesz belőle tízet. Ám amikor megkóstolja, meglepődik, hogy egy másik étellel találkozik, ezért mindet kidobja. Ezek ritka bakik, amiken segít a jelen lévő tanár, és rászól arra, aki túl sokat szed egyszerre.
Sokan panaszkodnak arra, hogy elfogy minden, mire leérnek ebédelni. Ez igazából nem lehetséges, mert ha az egyik fogás kifogy is, akkor úgynevezett puffercsomagot bontanak, így mindig ugyanannyi választási lehetőség marad. Előfordulhat, hogy az a fogás fogy el, amire éppen az adott gyerek vágyik. Ha arra készült, hogy rántott valamit eszik, de csak rizses hús van, akkor persze csalódott lehet. Az is kiszámíthatatlan, hogy miből esznek majd sokat. Feljegyzik, ha az egyik alkalommal hamar elfogyott egy ételfajta, majd legközelebb őrült nagy adagot rendelnek belőle, mégis előfordul, hogy másodszor már mégsem lesz annyira népszerű – és akkor megint maradék képződik, ami nem jó.
A szabadszedés nagy előnye, hogy sokkal kevesebb maradék kerül a kukába. Ebben segít az is, hogy a politechnikumban evés után a gyerekek a tányérjukat nem egyszerűen leteszik tálcástul, hanem nekik kell a tányérról eltávolítani azt, amit meghagytak. Így jobban szembesülnek azzal, mennyivel szedtek többet az igényeiknél, sőt a körülöttük állók is látják, ami motiválja őket arra, hogy legközelebb figyeljenek rá, hogy ne szedjenek túlságosan sokat – zárta gondolatait Kováts Lívia.
Sok gyerek szereti a szabadszedéses rendszert, néhányan kevésbé, az iskolát nehézségek elé állítja, több szülő szerint remek ötlet, de még rengeteg fejlesztésre van szükség ahhoz, hogy gördülékenyen működjön. Legfőbb tanulságnak az látszik, hogy a gyerekeknek sokkal többet kellene a táplálkozásról is tanítani, hogy egyáltalán ismerjék az ételeket, felismerjék az alapanyagokat, és tudják, mi a jó nekik, mi kevésbé.
2022-ben nagy cikksorozatban vettük végig a hazai közétkeztetés problémáit.

title: La Cruz Roja Venezolana asistió a más de 24 mil personas a tres meses de los terremotos
content:
A tres meses de los terremotos del 24 de junio, la Cruz Roja Venezolana asistió a más de 6 mil familias, unas 24 mil personas, con distribución de insumos de primera necesidad, kits de higiene y de cocina, así como artículos para la potabilización del agua.
La operación comenzó con un hospital de campaña en La Guaira y un punto de salud en la plaza Padre Machado de Maiquetía. Posteriormente, incorporó nuevas modalidades de respuesta, entre ellas las visitas médicas domiciliarias, jornadas de atención médica y ahora el Punto Comunitario, ubicado en el balneario de Catia La Mar.
Esta evolución responde a un proceso permanente de evaluación y a las más de 500 retroalimentaciones recibidas de las comunidades. La información recopilada permite a los equipos conocer las situaciones que persisten, identificar prioridades y definir las actividades y servicios que se desarrollan en cada localidad.
Servicios que permanecen activos de la Cruz Roja Venezolana
La Sociedad Nacional mantiene activos distintos centros para facilitar el acceso a servicios esenciales en La Guaira. Entre ellos se encuentran los puntos de hidratación del hospital de campaña de Macuto, la plaza Padre Machado de Maiquetía, el campamento transitorio de Ciudad Caribia y el ambulatorio Las Salinas.
En Catia La Mar, la Sociedad Nacional inauguró un Punto Comunitario en el balneario de la localidad con el apoyo de Banesco.
El lugar cuenta con una programación que incluye apoyo psicosocial cara a cara, primeros auxilios psicológicos, actividades recreativas para niños, niñas y adolescentes, espacios para personas mayores y charlas sobre salud, protección, higiene y autocuidado. También dispone de servicios para facilitar el acceso a agua segura, así como baños y duchas para las familias.
El Punto Comunitario funciona de lunes a viernes, de 8:00 am a 5:00 pm, de acuerdo con la programación establecida por los equipos de la Cruz Roja Venezolana.
Una operación sostenida por el voluntariado
Más de 1.600 voluntarios de 24 filiales han participado en las distintas etapas de la respuesta, con equipos que se han desplazado desde diferentes regiones del país para apoyar las acciones en las zonas afectadas.
Esta coordinación ha permitido integrar perfiles y capacidades distintas en jornadas médicas, visitas domiciliarias, distribuciones, actividades comunitarias y servicios de agua segura.
La movilización de voluntarios también ha permitido mantener una presencia constante en los puntos de atención y acompañar la evolución de la operación durante estos tres meses.

title: Kenya: Better Prices Lure Kitui Farmers Back to Cotton - If Seed, Rain and Young Farmers Follow
content:
The landscape changes as the road winds into Kitui County.
The green that often signals the beginning of Kenya's agricultural heartlands is hard to find here. Instead, the land stretches beneath a harsh sun, dotted with thorny bushes, sisal and the occasional baobab tree rising above the dry plains.
For miles, there is little indication that this is farmland.
But beneath the dry shrubs and sandy soils, farmers are preparing to plant a crop that has survived the changing fortunes of the region for generations.

Kitui is classified as a semi-arid county, and farming here has always been a gamble with the weather. Rainfall is unreliable, temperatures can be unforgiving and a single failed season can wipe out months of work.
Yet for a group of farmers in the county, cotton remains one of the few crops capable of turning this difficult terrain into an income-generating asset.
Our journey into Kitui's cotton country begins at Mosa Shopping Centre along the Kibwezi-Mombasa highway.
On this particular day, the centre is unusually quiet. There are no crowds of farmers, traders or produce sellers. It is not market day, so activity is limited.
We are met by Mutuku Mulei, chairman of the Kitui Rural Farmers Cooperative, together with several cooperative members. After introductions, we leave the highway and head deeper into the villages.
The farms are not immediately obvious.
They are tucked between dry shrubs and sandy paths, blending almost seamlessly into the surrounding landscape.
There are, however, small signs that the land has recently received a little relief from the dry conditions. Patches of wet sand can be seen along the edges of the roads, evidence that the previous night brought some rain.
For farmers here, even such small showers carry significance.
But there is little cotton to see.
Mulei explains that the timing of our visit coincides with land preparation, rather than the height of the cotton-growing season. The fields are therefore largely empty, although remnants of the previous crop remain.
It is also a reminder of how easily cotton farming can disappear from the landscape when farmers lose confidence in the crop.
For years, poor prices, delayed inputs and problems at ginneries pushed many farmers away from cotton.
“Many farmers had given up on cotton because of poor prices and mismanagement at the ginneries,” Mulei says. However the Agriculture and Food Authority is building the capacities of local groups to feed raw lint straight into thriving local industries like the Kitui County Textile Centre (KICOTEC).
The Kitui Rural Farmers Cooperative currently has about 70 members, down from 85 approximately three years ago.
For a crop already battling unpredictable weather, losing farmers creates another problem: the production base becomes smaller just when the industry needs more farmers to participate.
But Mulei believes confidence could be returning.
The price of cotton has increased from KSh54 to KSh72 per kilogramme which is the government's gazetted minimum price over the last three years giving farmers a reason to reconsider the crop.
The stakes reach well beyond Kitui. Kenya’s domestic cotton lint production has experienced a steady recovery, rising from 1,300 tonnes in 2021 to roughly 8,800 tonnes (approx. 25,000 bales) Local supply satisfies less than 15% of manufacturer needs. To bridge this gap, Kenya is forced to spend hard currency to import massive quantities of cotton and yarn from neighboring Tanzania and Uganda. Across the continent, governments and financiers are betting that more of Africa's cotton can be ginned, spun and turned into garments within Africa, and traded across borders under the African Continental Free Trade Area, rather than exported raw. That ambition ultimately depends on farms like these.
He has been encouraging cooperative members to increase their acreage to at least one acre this season.
Most farmers have traditionally cultivated half an acre or less, largely because of the high cost of production and uncertainty over rainfall.
For Mulei, however, the current season presents an opportunity.
Weather forecasts pointing to more reliable rainfall in the coming weeks have also raised expectations among farmers.
“If the rains come as predicted, we are hopeful of getting better yields,” says Mulei.
But in Kitui, optimism has to contend with a familiar list of problems.
One of the biggest is access to quality seed.
The Kitui County Ministry of Agriculture, Water and Livestock Development collaborates with national bodies to coordinate distribution of the hybrid BT cotton seed variety to local registered farmers. Mulei says "farmers received poor-quality seed last season, and even that seed arrived late."
For a crop whose performance depends heavily on timely planting, delays at the beginning of the season can have consequences all the way to harvest.
The same problem has affected pesticides.
According to Mulei, inadequate or delayed access to pesticides resulted in pest attacks that affected almost half of the crop last season.
The impact was not only on quantity but also on quality.
Cotton that might otherwise have achieved Grade 1 quality was downgraded to Grade 2. Grade 2 typically trades at a discount compared to the top-grade minimum, ranging between KES 45 to KES 52/kg depending on local ginnery negotiations and quality.
For farmers already operating on narrow margins, every downgrade represents money lost.
Unlike farmers in areas with more dependable rainfall, Kitui farmers cannot simply rely on one crop to carry them through an entire season.
They have developed ways of spreading the risk.
One of those strategies is intercropping cotton with green grams.
It may look like an ordinary farming practice, but for these farmers it is also a financial survival mechanism.
Cotton can take 5 to 6 months to mature, meaning farmers must wait for a considerable period before receiving returns from their crop.
Green grams, on the other hand, mature in roughly three months.
The proceeds from the green grams therefore provide farmers with money while they wait for cotton.
It is a simple form of diversification, but in a semi-arid environment where farmers cannot afford to wait without income, it can make the difference between remaining in cotton farming and abandoning it altogether.
The cooperative itself has become another layer of support.
Solomon Mulu, the cooperative secretary, says membership provides farmers with access to knowledge as well as financial opportunities.
The cooperative regularly organises training sessions with various players in the cotton value chain, including the county government.
The sessions focus on the practical aspects of cotton production, from land preparation and spacing to input application, weeding, pest management and harvesting.
“The training has helped farmers understand the best management practices required in growing cotton,” M ulei says.
The county government has also supported farmers with knapsack sprayers.
In addition, young people have been trained to offer spraying services to farmers at a reduced fee.
It is a model that addresses two problems at once: helping farmers manage pests while creating an opportunity for youth to earn an income from the agricultural value chain.
But the issue of young people in cotton farming remains a bigger concern.
Most of the cooperative's members are over 50 years old.
For Mulu, this is a warning sign about the future of cotton production in the county.
Young farmers are generally attracted to crops that offer quicker returns.
Green grams and sunflower, which mature relatively quickly, are therefore more appealing to many young people than cotton, which requires patience before a farmer sees the rewards.
The challenge is not necessarily that young people have rejected agriculture.
Rather, they are making economic choices.
A young farmer looking for income within a few months may struggle to see the attraction of committing land, labour and inputs to a crop that could take almost a year to mature.
Mulu believes that this is where government policy could make a difference.
He wants the county and national governments to explore ways of incentivising young people to take up cotton farming.
For him, the crop still has considerable economic potential.
“There is no other cash crop in Kitui apart from cotton,” he says, arguing that production in Kenya remains low compared with other cotton-producing countries.
The cooperative is also trying to build a financial cushion for its members.
Farmers contribute KSh2 from every kilogramme of cotton sold at KSh72 per kilogramme.
There is also a compulsory annual contribution of KSh1,500 per member.
The money goes towards strengthening the cooperative's savings base, which members can eventually access through loans.
The loans can help farmers purchase inputs and maintain their farms while waiting for harvest.
For small-scale farmers, that waiting period can be one of the most difficult parts of cotton production.
A farmer may have already spent money preparing land, purchasing inputs and paying for labour, yet the income from cotton remains months away.
Access to cooperative credit can therefore provide a bridge between planting and harvest.
But even with improved prices, training and cooperative support, Kitui's greatest challenge remains erratic rainfall.
Mulei says changing weather patterns have significantly disrupted farming in the region.
Rainfall is becoming increasingly unpredictable.
Sometimes the problem is not simply too little rain.
When rain eventually arrives, it can come with such intensity that it washes away the very soil farmers depend on.
Soil erosion has therefore become a major concern.
Mulei is encouraging farmers to construct gabions and terraces to control runoff and prevent flood water from destroying their fields.
He also advocates for proper land preparation.
Using an ox-plough, he says, can help break the hard pan beneath the soil, allowing crop roots to penetrate deeper.
Deeper roots can give plants better access to moisture while helping anchor them more firmly in the soil.
The goal is not merely to plant more cotton, but to build farms capable of surviving the increasingly unpredictable conditions.
It is a lesson that farmers across Kenya's drylands are learning: climate resilience is becoming as important as the choice of crop itself.
The county may not look like a conventional cotton-growing region.
There are no endless green fields stretching into the horizon. Much of the landscape appears better suited to thorny vegetation than commercial agriculture.
But cotton has an advantage here.
It is a crop that can perform under conditions where some of the crops traditionally associated with smallholder farming struggle.
Mulei and his fellow farmers see this as an opportunity.
Young people, meanwhile, need an economic reason to see cotton as more than an old man's crop.
The cooperative's shrinking membership is a warning, but the recent increase in cotton prices offers a reason for optimism.
The challenge now is turning that optimism into production.
Whether that happens will depend on more than rain: on seed and pesticides arriving on time, on ginneries and buyers that pay promptly, on finance that bridges the long wait to harvest, and on giving young farmers a reason to stay.
As we leave the farms around Mosa, the contrast is striking.
The landscape remains dry. The thorn bushes remain. The baobabs stand scattered across the horizon, while the sandy soil continues to bear the scars of years of erratic rainfall.
There is no lush cotton field to photograph yet.
Instead, what we find is something less visible but perhaps more important — farmers preparing the ground for another attempt.

title: Screen time isn’t linked to language delays in autistic children, large U.S. study finds
content:
A recent study suggests that reading books together at home is associated with better language abilities in young autistic children. The research provides evidence that this shared reading time helps explain why children from higher-income families tend to have stronger communication skills, but finds that screen time does not have a negative impact on these abilities. The findings were published in Autism Research.
Language skills vary widely among children on the autism spectrum. Autism is a developmental condition characterized by differences in social communication and restricted or repetitive behaviors. Some autistic children experience challenges producing or understanding spoken language, whereas others develop abilities similar to or exceeding those of their neurotypical peers. To understand this variation, scientists are increasingly looking at environmental influences that shape early development.
Human development is shaped by different layers of a child’s environment. Broad, distant factors include a family’s socioeconomic status, which generally refers to household income and the parents’ education levels. Closer, everyday factors include the specific activities a child experiences at home, such as shared book reading and screen time. Shared book reading involves an adult caregiver looking at and reading a story with a child, encouraging them to actively participate.
Screen time refers to the hours a child spends in front of televisions, tablets, computers, or smartphones. In the general population, researchers have observed that reading together provides benefits for communication skills. For example, a 2026 study of early childhood development indicated that interactive home literacy routines, like reading books and discussing past events, directly promote language growth over time.
However, reading with an autistic child might look different. In fact, a study covered by PsyPost in 2024 indicated that autistic children tend to focus their attention differently during shared reading than neurotypical children, looking less at the reader’s face and more at background objects. Because autistic children might engage with their environment in unique ways, scientists wanted to see if the typical patterns seen in other children hold true for them.
“Children with autism are likely to experience language delays and other challenges using and/or understanding spoken language that emerge early in childhood and sometimes persist into adulthood,” said lead author Meredith Pecukonis, an assistant professor in the Department of Psychology at Smith College and director of the Autism & Neurodevelopment (AND) Lab. “Identifying how certain aspects of the home environment relate to language abilities in autistic children is an important first step towards understanding how children’s experiences at home are shaping their language development, and developing interventions that lead to stronger language outcomes for autistic children.”
“Prior to publication of our study, only three studies had looked at the association between screen time and language abilities in autistic children,” Pecukonis told PsyPost. “All of these studies were conducted in China, and therefore no studies had been done in the U.S. on this topic. This gap in the literature was surprising to us, given that several studies have linked excessive screen time to language delays in neurotypical children, and autistic children engage in more screen time than their neurotypical peers.”
To address this gap, the researchers aimed to map out how socioeconomic status, reading habits, and screen use connect to language development. They wanted to see if the broader impact of a family’s income and education might operate through the daily routines children experience at home. To investigate this, the researchers analyzed data from the National Survey of Children’s Health collected between 2018 and 2022.
They focused on a nationally representative group of 1,217 autistic children living in the United States. The children in the sample were between the ages of two and five. Data was collected through surveys completed by parents or adult caregivers who lived with the children.
The survey assessed socioeconomic status by recording the highest level of parent education and calculating the family’s poverty ratio based on their income. It also tracked daily habits, asking parents how many days per week they read to their child and how many hours per weekday the child spent on electronic devices. To measure language, the researchers looked at both expressive and receptive skills.
Expressive language included abilities like speaking single words, asking questions, and telling a story. Receptive language involved understanding instructions, pointing to objects, and recognizing the beginning sounds of words. The statistical models accounted for both the age and sex of the children.
The results showed that autistic children from households with a higher socioeconomic status tended to have higher expressive and receptive language skills. These children were also read to more often and spent less time using screens. The researchers found a direct association between reading frequency and communication abilities. Autistic children who experienced more shared book reading at home demonstrated better language skills across the board.
When analyzing the connections between these variables, the researchers found that shared book reading partially explained the link between socioeconomic status and language skills. This suggests that children from higher-income families experience more frequent shared reading, which in turn helps build their communication abilities. The daily habit of reading acts as a bridge connecting a family’s broader resources to a child’s specific developmental gains.
“Effect sizes are small, meaning that the environment has a small yet significant impact on language development in autism,” Pecukonis said. “Parents raising children in lower SES households may have less time and energy to devote to shared book reading if they are working multiple jobs to pay their bills. Lower SES households may also have reduced access to books in the home.”
“If we want to support autistic children’s language development, we need to acknowledge that children are shaped by various aspects of their environments,” she continued. While some aspects can be addressed through direct family interventions, she noted that others “will likely require systemic change through public policy (e.g., providing greater financial support and services to lower SES families).”
The study found that screen time was not statistically associated with expressive or receptive language skills in autistic children. This means that the amount of time these children spent on devices did not predict better or worse communication abilities. This lack of an association stood out to the researchers, as previous studies of neurotypical children frequently link heavy screen use to developmental delays.
“We were really surprised that the association between amount of screen time and children’s language abilities was non-significant,” Pecukonis said. “This contradicts with what has been reported in the literature on neurotypical children.”
“The non-significant association between screen time and language abilities doesn’t suggest that screen time is ‘good’ or ‘bad’ for autistic children… it just shows that there is no association,” she added.
The results are in tension with research covered by PsyPost earlier this year, which found that replacing shared reading with screen time was linked to lower developmental scores. However, that earlier study looked at neurotypical preschoolers, whereas the new study focused exclusively on autistic children. Similarly, a 2024 study linked higher screen time to poorer language skills in the general population, which contrasts with the neutral effect observed here for autistic children.
As with all research, there are some caveats to consider. The study relied on parent surveys, which can sometimes be subject to reporting biases, such as overestimating reading time or underestimating screen use. The data also captured a single snapshot in time rather than tracking the children over many years. Because of this, it is not possible to declare that reading directly causes better language skills in this group.
“We only looked at two household activities (shared book reading and screen time) as our measures of the environment when in reality there are probably hundreds, if not thousands, of other aspects of the environment that are shaping language development in autism that we just didn’t measure here,” Pecukonis explained.
“The purpose of this work isn’t to ‘blame’ parents for their children’s language delays, but rather to document trends, show that the environment does matter for language development, and find ways to support autistic children through modifications to their environment,” she emphasized. “Our hope is that these findings will ultimately help autistic children and their families by showing that there is a need for greater support for those from lower SES households.”
The study also measured the sheer quantity of screen time and reading without looking at the quality of those activities. It is entirely possible that autistic children with stronger language skills are more likely to request story time, leading to more frequent reading sessions. Future studies could use direct observation to see how the types of digital media and the specific reading strategies parents use shape language development.
“We just applied for funding to run a longitudinal study to see how screen time measured early in development relates to language abilities measured later in development,” Pecukonis noted. “This study will also measure both the quantity and quality of screen time.”
The study, “Socioeconomic Status and Quantity of Shared Book Reading, But Not Screen Time, are Positively Associated With Language Skills in a Nationally Representative Sample of Autistic Children,” was authored by M. Pecukonis and A. Geffin.

title: Houston now requires air conditioning in all rentals, making cooling a housing standard
content:
In one of Texas' hottest major cities, air conditioning is no longer an optional perk for renters.
Houston City Council voted to require landlords to provide cooling in every rental unit, making AC a basic housing standard.
Here's what to know
Landlords now have 120 days — until December — to equip every rental unit with some form of cooling, according to the Houston Chronicle, whether it be central air, a window AC, or a portable unit.
Council approved the ordinance 12-2, ending Houston's longstanding "window screen exemption." Under that rule, owners could satisfy housing-code standards with screened windows and doors instead of refrigerated air.
In a city where intense summer heat can threaten people's health, that exception became increasingly notable. Going forward, a unit without AC will be handled through the normal code-enforcement system where residents can file a complaint, the health department can inspect the property, and landlords who do not fix the issue can face citations or end up in municipal court.
Backers of the change say it puts Houston in line with other big Texas cities and recognizes cooling as part of a safe, livable home rather than a luxury amenity.
More background
The change comes after several years of record summer heat, coinciding with an increase in heat-related deaths in the Houston area. Indoor cooling can make a major difference for older adults, children, and people with health conditions that get worse in extreme heat.
A 2023 survey put the number of rental households without air conditioning across the Houston metro at 20,400. But that estimate includes homes outside Houston city limits, so not all of those units would be covered by the ordinance.
The Houston fight is also part of a broader Texas debate. State lawmakers tried to create a statewide requirement for air conditioning in rentals, but that effort stalled amid objections to adding more regulations for property owners.
Some Houston officials expressed similar worries. Mayor John Whitmire said he was "fearful" the rule could increase rents and utility bills, while Council Member Twila Carter said, "My concern is for the people that this policy is intended to protect. This comes at a heavy cost, and it will put people on the streets."
What's being done?
Amy Peck, a council member and realtor, said Houston already requires heat even though it had never required air conditioning. She also said renters often had little recourse when an existing AC unit broke and was not repaired.
The ordinance was backed not just by housing advocates but also by the Houston Apartment Association, and there was no apparent landlord opposition during public hearings.
Julia Orduña of Texas Housers explained, "It comes down to that right to choose how much you're going to pay for electricity. It's not about living with or without AC in your unit, it's about deciding when to turn the AC on and off."
Council Member Alejandra Salinas said, "All Houstonians deserve a right to rest from heat, and that's what this ordinance is going to do."

title: 63 sociale woningen ingehuldigd in voormalig industrieel gebouw in Vorst
content:
In het voormalige industriële gebouw Luttre in de gemeente Vorst zijn woensdag 63 sociale woningen ingehuldigd door Zuiderhaard en de Brusselse Gewestelijke Huisvestingsmaatschappij (BGHM). Het herbestemmingsproject op de hoek van de Luttrebruglaan en de Gerijstraat beslaat een oppervlakte van 11.000 vierkante meter.
63 sociale woningen ingehuldigd in voormalig industrieel gebouw in Vorst
Het gebouw, dat vroeger door het bedrijf Diamant Boart werd gebruikt, werd aangekocht in 2016 en verbouwd door het architechtenbureau Matador/CLN. Dat legde de nadruk op het behoud van bestaande structuren, het beperken van sloopwerkzaamheden en het hergebruik van materialen.
De 63 appartementen beschikken over één tot zes slaapkamers, een loggia en een wintertuin. Nieuwe houtstructuren zorgen voor thermische en geluidsisolatie. Op de begane grond zijn nieuwe kantoren voor sociale vastgoedmaatschappij Zuiderhaard en een gemeenschappelijke polyvalente ruimte voorzien.
Mooi voorbeeld
Dorien Robben, adjunct-directeur-generaal van de BGHM, spreekt van een "mooi voorbeeld van herbestemming van een voormalig industrieel gebouw tot moderne en comfortabele woningen". Zowel het behouden van het architecturaal erfgoed als het ontwikkelen van sociale woningen is volgens haar noodzakelijk.
Matthieu Tihon en Samira Benallal, voorzitter en vicevoorzitter van Zuiderhaard, zien in de herbestemming van voormalige industriële sites een antwoord op de huisvestingscrisis in het Brussels Hoofdstedelijk Gewest.
Ook Karine Lalieux (PS), de Brusselse staatssecretaris bevoegd voor Huisvesting, juicht het project toe. Zij is van mening dat sociale woningen zowel via nieuwbouw als via de renovatie en herbestemming van bestaande gebouwen moet gebeuren.

title: Ladakh LG clears withdrawal of cases against 20 in September 24 violence
content:
Srinagar: Ladakh LG VK Saxena approved Wednesday withdrawal of cases against 20 of the 81 people who faced criminal charges for “rioting and arson” after violent statehood protests in Leh last Sept 24 that left four people dead in police firing and wounded nearly 90.“The cases have been withdrawn under section 360 of BNSS on the recommendation of Ladakh police following a comprehensive review of the status of investigations into the cases,” a govt spokesperson said.Of 87 accused identified in rioting cases, 81 were arrested and criminal proceedings initiated against them. Following the review, police recommended withdrawal of charges against 20, the spokesperson said. LG’s office did not comment on the status of the remaining 61 accused.LG’s office called the move significant for peace, public tranquillity and social harmony in Ladakh. On Sept 13, Saxena sanctioned Rs 15 lakh compensation to the next of kin of each of the four dead. He also approved ex gratia of Rs 3 lakh for those with major wounds and Rs 1 lakh for minor injuries.
On Sept 24 last year, police opened fire after protests demanding statehood and Sixth Schedule status for Ladakh turned violent.
Authorities imposed curfew-like restrictions, suspended mobile internet and arrested 81 people.Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance later refused talks with Union govt until a judicial inquiry commission was announced. On Oct 17, 2025, Union home ministry announced a judicial probe, with the commission begging work on Oct 27. It is yet to submit its report.After the probe was announced, Centre held talks with LAB and KDA representatives. Ladakh groups said Centre had assured withdrawal of cases against those arrested in Sept 2025 and compensation for victims and those wounded.

title: Le couple dont le mariage a été refusé à Béziers en 2023 s'est marié en Algérie cet été
content:
Le couple dont le mariage a été refusé à Béziers en 2023 s'est marié en Algérie cet été
Le couple dont le maire de Béziers (Hérault) avait refusé le mariage en 2023 s'est marié cet été en Algérie, a appris franceinfo mercredi. Robert Ménard n'avait pas souhaité célébrer l'union entre un Algérien sous obligation de quitter le territoire et une Française.
Le couple, que le maire de Béziers (Hérault) Robert Ménard avait refusé de marier en 2023 car l'homme était visé par une OQTF, s'est finalement marié cet été en Algérie, a appris franceinfo d'une source proche du dossier, confirmant une information de BFMTV.
Il y a trois ans, le 7 juillet 2023, Robert Ménard avait refusé de marier Mustapha, citoyen algérien, avec Eva, une ressortissante française, soupçonnant un mariage blanc. Mustapha, en France depuis l'âge de 16 ans, faisait l'objet d'une obligation de quitter le territoire délivrée en août 2022. Il avait finalement été expulsé le 20 juillet vers l'Algérie.
Les deux époux avaient porté plainte contre l'édile, qui doit être jugé le 30 septembre prochain pour cette affaire au tribunal judiciaire de Montpellier. Le mariage de Mustapha et d'Eva a eu lieu le 14 juillet dernier, à Bir El Djir, une commune située près d'Oran, dans le nord-ouest de l'Algérie.
Cette union est accueillie "avec beaucoup d'émotion" par l'avocate du couple, Maître Vanessa Edberg. "Après plus de trois années d’épreuves et de séparation, ils ont enfin pu accomplir ce qui devait être, dès l’origine, un acte relevant simplement de leur vie privée et familiale", écrit l'avocate à franceinfo. "Au-delà de la procédure judiciaire, je suis heureuse que [le couple] puissent enfin reprendre possession de [son] histoire", conclut Vanessa Edberg.
